pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and value 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts exact list ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'].
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and asserts only those, in id order, with status 200.
'AC-4' test checks / and /?show=all give the full list in id order.

The test 'AC-5: each view links to the other' asserts both links, so it would fail if either were removed. The spec's own 'verified by review: checked by hand' marker is a non-step, but a test covers the item. The late edit to the item is reported separately.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; the 'AC-7' test asserts it.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits', github-actions bot) rewrote acceptance item AC-5 after the owner's go (2026-10-12). It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence, which breaks the sentence and now splits it from its continuation 'starred list.'. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this. 'Checked by hand' is also not a followable step. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit. The item is already covered by a test, so no review marker is needed. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR body claims 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edits AC-5. The body doesn't mention it.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit, or disclose it in the PR body with the owner's approval.

findings.what: The README doesn't mention `?show=all`, the 400 for other values, or the ★ marker. The first two are in the PR text.
findings.fix: Optionally add a short line about the 400 for invalid `show` values.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. No extra behaviour found beyond loosening the traffic route check to allow query strings, which the PR discloses and tests.
All seven acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. All four state-table rows have tests. AC-5 was edited after the go with no recorded decision (high finding).

Tests assert real behaviour (exact lists, 400 statuses, DB CHECK). I did not run them (the Workers test pool and its dependencies are not available here); CI covers that. The traffic fake app and tests/traffic-config.test.sh were updated and cover the query and the rejected space and fragment.
The README was updated for the starred view. Only a minor omission (low finding).
Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup against __proto__, and the SQL has no user input. No defects found.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the view comes from a fixed allow-list, and the SQL is static. The spec edit comes from an automation bot but contains no instructions aimed at the reviewer.
The diff touches no UI files beyond server-rendered HTML in src/index.js; there are no styles or components, and nothing was designed beyond the specified links.
There is no browser or UI flow to exercise here. HTML output is covered by the Worker tests.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false because of the AC-5 edit. The title is within 72 characters.
